title: Vacuum Toilet Assembly — Flush Cycle and Seat Interface Check

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Servicing check of one vacuum toilet assembly, covering the flush cycle, the interface seal seating gap and, on post modification aircraft, the latch closing force that sets the seal compression.

sections.purpose: This task gives the servicing check of one vacuum toilet assembly at the scheduled interval or after an odour complaint, and gives the seating gap and latch force limits used to decide whether the interface seal is serviceable.
sections.job_setup_note: Do the check with the waste tank at less than half full, so that the flush cycle is representative. Put the lavatory out of service and post the notice. Get the feeler gauge set and, on aircraft with the low force latch, the latch force gauge. A seating gap outside the limit is a seal replacement, not an adjustment; there is no adjustment on either latch standard.
sections.procedure: 1. Put the lavatory out of service and post the notice on the door. 2. Do three flush cycles and listen for airflow at the bowl to shroud interface after the cycle ends. 3. WARNING: DO NOT PUT YOUR HAND INTO THE BOWL DURING A FLUSH CYCLE. THE VACUUM IS SUFFICIENT TO TRAP A HAND. 4. Open the shroud access and examine the interface seal for compression set, splitting and displacement. 5. Measure the seating gap at four points around the interface with the feeler gauge. The gap must be less than 0.4 millimetres at every point. 6. On aircraft post MOD-168074, measure the latch closing force with the gauge and confirm it is between 40 and 70 newtons. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT INCREASE THE LATCH FORCE TO CLOSE A SEATING GAP. AN OVER-CENTRED LATCH TAKES A PERMANENT SET IN THE SEAL AND THE GAP RETURNS WORSE. 8. Check the harness behind the shroud is tied clear of the partition bracket. 9. Close the shroud access and do one further flush cycle. 10. Confirm no airflow is audible at the interface.
sections.close_out: Return the lavatory to service and remove the notice. Clean the work area with the approved agent. Record the seating gaps, the latch force where applicable and the flush cycle result in the cabin defect log.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; step 6 applies to aircraft post MOD-168074 only

safety_precautions: Do not put your hand into the bowl during a flush cycle.
Put the lavatory out of service and post the notice before you start.
